newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Feb 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Feb 13.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Burmese Army has launched a major military offensive against Karen rebel strongholds along the Thai-Burmese border, driving thousands of refugees into the Umphang district of Thailand's northern Tak province. The operation on Wednesday, which targeted the headquarters of the Karen National Union and neighbouring areas under its control, came on the same day that the Burmese ruling junta informed Thailand of its decision to use force against the rebel ethnic group. (THE NATION)

- The opposition has threatened to discuss in Parliament the government's failure to prosecute Bangkok Bank of Commerce's former management on banking law charges, following yesterday's decision by public prosecutors to drop them because the statutory period has expired. Charges have been traded between the Attorney General's Office and the police following the announcement of the decision which the opposition described as a farce. (THE NATION)

- Education Minister Sukhavich Rangsitphol plans to counter the opposition's parliamentary onslaught today with claims that the bloc is attacking him in collusion with some sore losers in computers-for-schools bidding. The House is set for a fierce debate over Sukhavich's controversial distribution of more than 5 million baht to about 100 MPs whose help he sought in surveying the needs of rural schools. (THE NATION) + + + +

- Thailand has agreed to reduce the deadline for tariff cuts on information technology (IT) products from 2007 to 2005 to comply with a request from trade counterparts, especially the Quad group. The country has also decided to take six products from the "Sensitive List," to the "Slow List," which will see the tariff for IT products reduced to zero by the year 2005. (THE NATION)

- Thailand is close to finalising large purchases of natural gas from Indonesia's vast Natuna field. Many of the terms have been agreed and sticking points over the price are being resolved. The contract would call for the delivery of one billion cubic feet per day of natural gas to the Thai state energy enterprise for 30 years, starting in 2002 or 2003. (BANGKOK POST)
